---
title: "09 - Random forest models of AGC and soil carbon"
output: html_document
params:
  use_cache: false
---

**Purpose.** Fits random forest regression models (tidymodels + ranger) of aboveground carbon stock (AGC) and soil organic carbon (SOC; by default the change from baseline, `use_soc_delta = T`) as functions of site, climate, management and prior land-use covariates. Rows whose site has no usable coordinates (and hence no ecoregion) are excluded. Missing values in the management and species-trait binaries are coded as an explicit "missing" category (one-hot encoded, so each variable contributes `= True`, `= False` and `= Missing` features) rather than imputed; remaining numeric predictors are median-imputed. Hyperparameters are tuned by cross-validation and performance is evaluated on a held-out test set. The fitted models are then interpreted with SHAP values and interactions (TreeSHAP), partial dependence plots (PDP) for the top predictors ranked by grouped mean |SHAP| (indicator columns summed per observation), and profiling of extreme predictions.

**Inputs.**

- `output/data/{agc,soc}_by_plot_and_age_w_covars_drop_outliers.xlsx` (from `04_drop_outliers.Rmd`)
- `output/tables/bivariate_model_summaries.xlsx` (from `05_bivariate_analysis.Rmd`), used to select the candidate predictors
- `data/groa_af/sites.csv` (GROA-AF dataset) and `output/intermediate/s3_by_plot.xlsx` (from `01`), used to identify rows whose site has coordinates

**Outputs.**

- Model cache: `output/intermediate/rf_model/{fit_list,test_data_list,perf_list}.rds`
- SHAP cache: `output/intermediate/shap_objects.rds`
- Tables (`output/tables/`): `rf_model_performance.csv` (original split), `rf_model_performance_repeated_splits.csv` and `rf_model_performance_summary.csv` (50 random splits; reported in the paper), `rf_shap_top_interaction_pairs.csv`
- Figures (`output/figures/`): `rf_pdp_top6.png`, `rf_pdp_top9_agc.png`, `rf_pdp_top9_soc.png`, `rf_model_diagnostics.png`, `rf_shap_interaction_heatmap.png`, `rf_shap_beeswarm.png`

**Caching and run time.** Model training (`run-rf`: 40-point grid x 10-fold CV x 2 pools, 500 trees each) is the most expensive step, followed by the SHAP interaction values (`shap-compute`) and the PDP section (which uses the SHAP ranking). With the `use_cache` YAML parameter `false` (the default) everything is computed and the fitted models and SHAP values are cached to `output/intermediate/`. Setting `use_cache: true` (or `Rscript run_all.R --use-cache`) skips training and SHAP computation and reloads the cached results (`load-model`, `shap-load`), which is useful for re-making tables and figures.

```{r setup}
library(here)
library(tidyverse)
library(openxlsx)
library(tidymodels)
library(ranger)
library(patchwork)
library(cowplot)     # PDP / diagnostic panel assembly
library(treeshap)    # SHAP values and interactions
library(ggbeeswarm)  # SHAP beeswarm plot

set.seed(7381)
```

---

## Configuration

```{r config}
# Set the use_cache param (YAML header) to TRUE to skip model training and SHAP
# computation and reuse the cached results in output/intermediate/ (requires
# one prior run with FALSE)
use_cache <- isTRUE(params$use_cache)

af_cats <- c('AC', 'BP', 'COP', 'FAL', 'FOD', 'MS', 'OTH_AF', 'PAR',
             'RB', 'ROT', 'SA', 'SP', 'SPC', 'TMC', 'WL')

c_data_names_rf <- c("agc", "soc")

only_bivariate_sig_vars <- F

# Select whether to use SOC stock or delta from baseline
use_soc_delta <- T

# 0/1 binaries with many NAs: recoded to "false" / "true" / "missing" so missingness
# is an explicit category rather than imputed
explicit_missing_bin_vars <- c(
  "pruning", "weed_control", "tillage", "grazing", "burning", "litter_management",
  "pest_control", "fertilizer", "irrigation",
  "n_fix_bin", "myco_fungi_am", "myco_fungi_ecm", "freezing_exposed"
)
# Exempt from step_nzv / step_other (ecoregion: keep all levels, incl. rare Boreal/polar)
no_filter_vars <- c(explicit_missing_bin_vars, "ecoregion")

```

## Load bivariate model summaries (once, before loop)

Predictor candidates for each pool are taken from the bivariate model summaries written by notebook 06.

```{r load-bivar}

bivar_sum_file_path <- here("output", "tables", "bivariate_model_summaries.xlsx")
bms_wb      <- loadWorkbook(bivar_sum_file_path)
sheet_names <- getSheetNames(bivar_sum_file_path)

```

---

## Sites with coordinates

Rows are kept only if their site has usable coordinates: a bounding-box centroid and an ecoregion in the sites table of the GROA-AF dataset (sites whose centroid is far outside the Audebert zones have no ecoregion). A row's site is that of its first plot found in `s3_by_plot`, the same rule 03a/03b use to join site covariates.

```{r site-coords}

sites_with_coords <- read.csv(here("data", "groa_af", "sites.csv"), na.strings = "", fileEncoding = "UTF-8-BOM",
                              colClasses = c(site_id = "character")) |>
  filter(!is.na(lat), !is.na(audebert_ecoregion_5class)) |>
  pull(site_id) |>
  as.character()

plot_site <- read.xlsx(here("output", "intermediate", "s3_by_plot.xlsx")) |>
  transmute(ssp_id, site_id = as.character(site_id))

row_site <- function(ssp_ids) {
  map_chr(str_split(ssp_ids, ", "), \(v) {
    s <- plot_site$site_id[match(trimws(v), plot_site$ssp_id)]
    s <- s[!is.na(s)]
    if (length(s) > 0) s[1] else NA_character_
  })
}

```

---

## Run RF pipeline for each carbon pool

For each pool: load data, select predictors from the bivariate summaries, make a stratified 80/20 train/test split, tune `mtry` and `min_n` over a 40-point Latin hypercube grid with 10-fold CV (the most expensive step in the notebook), fit the final model on the training set, and evaluate it on the test set.

```{r run-rf, eval = !use_cache}

reg_metrics <- metric_set(rmse, rsq, mae)

perf_list       <- list()
fit_list        <- list()
test_data_list  <- list()

for (c_data_name in c_data_names_rf) {

  outcome <- if (grepl("change", c_data_name)) "c_t_ha_yr" else "c_t_ha"

  cat("\n====", toupper(c_data_name), "====\n")

  # --- Load data ---
  df <- read.xlsx(paste0(here("output", "data"), "/", c_data_name,
                         "_by_plot_and_age_w_covars_drop_outliers.xlsx")) |>
    filter(af_cat %in% af_cats) |>
    # Binary dummy columns use 1/NA encoding; replace NA with 0 so step_impute_median
    # does not incorrectly impute absent categories as present
    mutate(across(
      (starts_with("prior_") | starts_with("ctrl_") | starts_with("soil_tex_")) & where(is.numeric),
      ~replace_na(., 0)
    ))
  
  
  # Drop rows whose site has no usable coordinates (see site-coords)
  has_coords <- row_site(df$ssp_id) %in% sites_with_coords
  cat("Dropping", sum(!has_coords), "rows without site coordinates\n")
  df <- df[has_coords, ]
  if (anyNA(df$ecoregion)) {
    stop(sum(is.na(df$ecoregion)), " rows have coordinates but no ecoregion; check 03a/03b joins")
  }

  # Explicit missing category instead of imputation
  bad_bin <- keep(explicit_missing_bin_vars, \(v) v %in% names(df) && any(!df[[v]] %in% c(0, 1, NA)))
  if (length(bad_bin) > 0) stop("Non-0/1 values in: ", paste(bad_bin, collapse = ", "))
  df <- df |>
    mutate(
      across(any_of(explicit_missing_bin_vars),
             \(x) case_when(x == 1 ~ "true", x == 0 ~ "false", is.na(x) ~ "missing"))
    )

  # Set soc c_t_ha as c_t_ha_delta if selected
  if (use_soc_delta && c_data_name == 'soc') {
    df <- df %>%
      mutate(c_t_ha = c_t_ha_delta) %>%
      select(-c_t_ha_delta)
  }
  
  
  cat("n =", nrow(df), "\n")

  # --- Identify bivariate-significant predictors ---
  sig_var_ls <- list()
  # 06 labels pools in c_pool as "AGC" / "\u0394SOC", not "agc" / "soc"
  bms_pool <- pool_labels[[c_data_name]]

  for (sheet_name in sheet_names) {
    bms_df <- readWorkbook(bms_wb, sheet = sheet_name)

    required_cols <- c("c_pool", "significance", "independent_var")
    if (length(setdiff(required_cols, names(bms_df))) > 0) {
      sig_var_ls[[sheet_name]] <- character(0)
      next
    }

    sig <- ifelse(is.na(bms_df$significance), "", as.character(bms_df$significance))

    keep_rows <- if (only_bivariate_sig_vars) {
      (bms_df$c_pool == bms_pool) & grepl("\\*", sig)
    } else {
      bms_df$c_pool == bms_pool
    }

    # For prior_cat: extract category names, excluding the 'Full model' summary row
    sig_var_ls[[sheet_name]] <- if (sheet_name == "prior_cat") {
      cats <- bms_df$category[keep_rows]
      cats[!cats %in% c("Full model", "unknown", NA)]
    } else {
      # Exclude 'Full model' summary rows if the category column exists
      rows <- if ("category" %in% names(bms_df)) {
        keep_rows & (is.na(bms_df$category) | bms_df$category != "Full model")
      } else {
        keep_rows
      }
      bms_df$independent_var[rows]
    }
  }

  sig_var_ls[["bin_var"]]   <- str_replace(sig_var_ls[["bin_var"]], " = 1", "")
  # Fail loudly if the pool label didn't match (would silently drop predictors)
  if (length(sig_var_ls[["cont_var"]]) == 0 || length(sig_var_ls[["prior_cat"]]) == 0) {
    stop("No predictors found for '", bms_pool, "' in ", bivar_sum_file_path,
         "; check that c_pool labels in 05 match pool_labels here.")
  }
  sig_var_ls[["prior_cat"]] <- paste0("prior_", sig_var_ls[["prior_cat"]])

  predictors <- unique(c(
    "af_cat",
    "ecoregion",
    sig_var_ls[["cont_var"]],
    sig_var_ls[["bin_var"]],
    sig_var_ls[["prior_cat"]],
    if (c_data_name == "soc") c("ctrl_CROP", "ctrl_GRA", "ctrl_OTH_CTR", "ctrl_chrono") else character(0)
  ))
  predictors <- setdiff(predictors, "depth_max")
  predictors <- union(predictors, "prior_unknown")

  cat("Predictors (", length(predictors), "):", paste(predictors, collapse = ", "), "\n")

  # --- Train / test split and CV folds ---
  set.seed(7381)
  data_split <- initial_split(df, prop = 0.8, strata = outcome)
  train_df   <- training(data_split)
  test_df    <- testing(data_split)

  set.seed(7381)
  cv_folds <- vfold_cv(train_df, v = 10, strata = outcome)

  cat("Train n:", nrow(train_df), " | Test n:", nrow(test_df), "\n")

  # --- Recipe ---
  base_formula <- as.formula(paste(outcome, "~", paste(predictors, collapse = " + ")))

  # Explicit-missing variables are exempt from step_nzv / step_other, which would
  # otherwise drop them (dominant "missing" level) or pool their rare levels.
  # One-hot so every level (incl. "missing" and the af_cat reference) is a feature.
  rf_recipe <- recipe(base_formula, data = train_df) |>
    step_nzv(all_predictors(), -any_of(no_filter_vars)) |>
    step_impute_median(all_numeric_predictors()) |>
    step_impute_mode(all_nominal_predictors()) |>
    step_other(all_nominal_predictors(), -any_of(no_filter_vars), threshold = 0.01) |>
    step_dummy(all_nominal_predictors(), one_hot = TRUE) |>
    step_zv(all_predictors())

  # --- Model spec ---
  rf_spec <- rand_forest(
    trees = 500,
    mtry  = tune(),
    min_n = tune()
  ) |>
    set_mode("regression") |>
    set_engine("ranger")

  # --- Workflow ---
  wf_rf <- workflow() |>
    add_recipe(rf_recipe) |>
    add_model(rf_spec)

  # --- Tune: Latin hypercube grid over mtry and min_n ---
  prepped_cols <- prep(rf_recipe) |> bake(new_data = NULL) |> ncol() - 1L

  rf_grid <- grid_latin_hypercube(
    mtry(range = c(2L, max(2L, floor(prepped_cols / 2L)))),
    min_n(),
    size = 40
  )

  set.seed(7381)
  rf_res <- tune_grid(
    wf_rf,
    resamples = cv_folds,
    grid      = rf_grid,
    metrics   = reg_metrics,
    control   = control_grid(save_pred = TRUE)
  )

  rf_params <- select_best(rf_res, metric = "rmse")
  cat("Best mtry:", rf_params$mtry, "| min_n:", rf_params$min_n, "\n")

  # --- Finalize and fit on full training set ---
  final_rf_wf  <- finalize_workflow(wf_rf, rf_params)
  final_rf_fit <- fit(final_rf_wf, data = train_df)

  # --- Evaluate on held-out test set ---
  test_metrics <- predict(final_rf_fit, new_data = test_df) |>
    bind_cols(test_df |> dplyr::select(all_of(outcome))) |>
    reg_metrics(truth = !!rlang::sym(outcome), estimate = .pred) |>
    pivot_wider(names_from = .metric, values_from = .estimate) |>
    mutate(
      c_pool = c_data_name,
      mtry   = rf_params$mtry,
      min_n  = rf_params$min_n
    ) |>
    dplyr::select(c_pool, rmse, rsq, mae, mtry, min_n)

  # Store results
  perf_list[[c_data_name]]      <- test_metrics
  fit_list[[c_data_name]]        <- final_rf_fit
  test_data_list[[c_data_name]]  <- list(train_df = train_df, df = test_df, outcome = outcome)

}

```

## Model performance

```{r performance}

perf_tbl <- bind_rows(perf_list) |>
  mutate(across(where(is.numeric), ~ round(., 3)))

perf_tbl |>
  mutate(c_pool = recode(c_pool, agc = "AGC", soc = "\u0394SOC"))

write_csv(perf_tbl, here("output", "tables", "rf_model_performance.csv"))

```

## Performance across random train/test splits

A single 80/20 split gives a noisy estimate of test performance, especially for ΔSOC. Each final model specification (tuned `mtry` and `min_n` fixed; recipe re-estimated on each training set) is refitted on 50 random 80/20 splits stratified on the outcome, and the test-set metrics are summarized. The paper reports these means. Hyperparameters were tuned once, on the original training set, so the estimates may be slightly optimistic. `num.threads` is fixed because ranger's results depend on it. Runs also with `use_cache` (about 4 minutes).

```{r repeated-splits}

n_splits <- 50
reg_metrics <- metric_set(rmse, rsq, mae)
set.seed(5126)
split_seeds <- sample.int(1e6, n_splits)

split_perf <- map_dfr(c("soc", "agc"), function(pool) {
  td      <- test_data_list[[pool]]
  outcome <- td$outcome
  full_df <- bind_rows(td$train_df, td$df)
  spec    <- extract_spec_parsnip(fit_list[[pool]]) |> set_engine("ranger", num.threads = 10)
  wf      <- workflow() |> add_recipe(extract_preprocessor(fit_list[[pool]])) |> add_model(spec)
  map_dfr(seq_along(split_seeds), function(i) {
    set.seed(split_seeds[i])
    sp <- initial_split(full_df, prop = 0.8, strata = all_of(outcome))
    f  <- fit(wf, data = training(sp))
    m  <- predict(f, new_data = testing(sp)) |>
      bind_cols(testing(sp) |> dplyr::select(all_of(outcome))) |>
      reg_metrics(truth = !!rlang::sym(outcome), estimate = .pred)
    tibble(c_pool = pool, split = i, seed = split_seeds[i],
           rmse = m$.estimate[m$.metric == "rmse"],
           rsq  = m$.estimate[m$.metric == "rsq"],
           mae  = m$.estimate[m$.metric == "mae"])
  })
})

split_perf_summary <- split_perf |>
  group_by(c_pool) |>
  summarise(n_splits = n(),
            across(c(rsq, rmse, mae), list(mean = mean, sd = sd, min = min, max = max)),
            .groups = "drop") |>
  arrange(c_pool)

split_perf_summary |>
  mutate(across(where(is.numeric) & !n_splits, ~ round(., 3)),
         c_pool = recode(c_pool, agc = "AGC", soc = "\u0394SOC"))

write_csv(split_perf, here("output", "tables", "rf_model_performance_repeated_splits.csv"))
write_csv(split_perf_summary, here("output", "tables", "rf_model_performance_summary.csv"))

```

---

## SHAP values and interactions

TreeSHAP values for every training observation, plus pairwise SHAP interaction values for a random subsample of 75 observations (interactions are O(n * p^2) and are the most expensive step in this section). The result is cached to `output/intermediate/shap_objects.rds` (see `shap-save` and `shap-load` below).

```{r shap-compute, eval = !use_cache}

shap_list       <- list()
shap_inter_list <- list()

for (pool in c_data_names_rf) {

  cat("\n=== SHAP:", toupper(pool), "===\n")

  fit      <- fit_list[[pool]]
  train_df <- test_data_list[[pool]]$train_df
  outcome  <- test_data_list[[pool]]$outcome

  # Bake training data through the fitted recipe to get the feature matrix
  prepped <- extract_recipe(fit)
  X_baked <- bake(prepped, new_data = train_df) |>
    select(-all_of(outcome))

  rf_engine <- extract_fit_engine(fit)
  unified   <- ranger.unify(rf_engine, X_baked)

  cat("Computing SHAP values (n =", nrow(X_baked), ")...\n")
  shap_obj          <- treeshap(unified, X_baked, verbose = FALSE)
  shap_list[[pool]] <- shap_obj

  # Interactions are O(n * p^2) — subsample to keep tractable
  n_inter <- min(75, nrow(X_baked))
  set.seed(7381)
  X_sub <- X_baked[sample(nrow(X_baked), n_inter), ]

  cat("Computing SHAP interactions (n =", n_inter, ")...\n")
  shap_inter_obj          <- treeshap(unified, X_sub, interactions = TRUE, verbose = FALSE)
  shap_inter_list[[pool]] <- shap_inter_obj

  cat("Done.\n")
}

```

## Predictor ranking by SHAP

One score per predictor: for each observation, the SHAP values of a categorical predictor's indicator columns (including its "missing" level) are summed, and the mean absolute value of that sum is taken across observations. For continuous predictors this is simply the mean absolute SHAP value. This ranking selects the predictors shown in the PDP figures and the extreme-prediction profiles.

```{r shap-rank}

shap_rank <- map_dfr(c_data_names_rf, function(pool) {
  shaps  <- as.data.frame(shap_list[[pool]]$shaps)
  parent <- coalesce(dummy_label_map$parent_var[match(names(shaps), dummy_label_map$dummy_col)],
                     names(shaps))
  # SHAP values are additive, so a predictor's contribution to one prediction is
  # the sum of its indicator columns; summing mean |SHAP| per column instead
  # would double-count levels that partly cancel within an observation.
  map_dbl(split(names(shaps), parent),
          \(cols) mean(abs(rowSums(shaps[, cols, drop = FALSE])))) |>
    enframe(name = "parent_var", value = "mean_abs_shap") |>
    left_join(predictor_label_lkup, by = c("parent_var" = "Variable")) |>
    transmute(c_pool = pool, parent_var, label = coalesce(Label, parent_var), mean_abs_shap) |>
    arrange(desc(mean_abs_shap)) |>
    mutate(rank = row_number())
})

shap_rank |> filter(rank <= 9)

```

Numbers cited in the text for the ΔSOC model: the SHAP contribution of degraded prior land use (training set) and how often pruning was reported (all modelled ΔSOC rows).

```{r cited-soc-numbers}

soc_shaps <- as.data.frame(shap_list$soc$shaps)
soc_baked <- bake(extract_recipe(fit_list$soc), new_data = test_data_list$soc$train_df)
stopifnot(nrow(soc_baked) == nrow(soc_shaps))
tibble(prior_degraded = soc_baked$prior_DEGRADED == 1, shap = soc_shaps$prior_DEGRADED) |>
  group_by(prior_degraded) |>
  summarise(n = n(), mean_shap = mean(shap), .groups = "drop")

bind_rows(test_data_list$soc$train_df, test_data_list$soc$df) |>
  count(pruning) |>
  mutate(pct = round(100 * n / sum(n), 1))
```

## Partial dependence plots — top 6 predictors per pool

```{r pdp-plots, fig.width = 9, fig.height = 10}

# Top 6 predictors per pool by grouped mean |SHAP| (shap-rank), in rank order
top6 <- shap_rank |>
  filter(rank <= 6) |>
  dplyr::select(c_pool, parent_var, label, rank) |>
  arrange(c_pool, rank)

# Levels of `var` kept by step_other in the fitted recipe (NULL if not pooled)
retained_levels <- function(fit, var) {
  rec <- extract_recipe(fit)
  i <- which(map_lgl(rec$steps, \(s) inherits(s, "step_other")))
  if (length(i) == 0) return(NULL)
  kept <- tidy(rec, number = i) |> filter(terms == var) |> pull(retained)
  if (length(kept) == 0) NULL else kept
}


# Manual PDP: for each grid value of the focal variable, replace that column in ALL
# training rows and average the workflow's predictions. Categorical levels that
# step_other pooled in the fitted recipe all get the same prediction, so they are
# shown as a single "rare_pooled" point.
compute_pdp <- function(fit, var, train_df, grid_n = 20) {
  pooled <- character(0)
  if (is.numeric(train_df[[var]])) {
    grid_vals <- seq(
      quantile(train_df[[var]], 0.02, na.rm = TRUE),
      quantile(train_df[[var]], 0.98, na.rm = TRUE),
      length.out = grid_n
    )
  } else {
    grid_vals <- sort(unique(na.omit(train_df[[var]])))
    kept   <- retained_levels(fit, var)
    pooled <- if (is.null(kept)) character(0) else setdiff(grid_vals, kept)
    if (length(pooled) > 0) grid_vals <- c(setdiff(grid_vals, pooled), pooled[1])
  }
  purrr::map_dfr(grid_vals, function(val) {
    nd <- train_df
    nd[[var]] <- val
    x_lab <- if (!is.numeric(val) && val %in% pooled) "rare_pooled" else val
    tibble(x_val = x_lab, yhat = mean(predict(fit, new_data = nd)$.pred, na.rm = TRUE))
  })
}

# Pass 1: compute all PDP data and store with metadata for shared y-limit calculation
pdp_data_list <- list()

for (pool in c_data_names_rf) {
  vars_df  <- top6 |> filter(c_pool == pool)
  fit      <- fit_list[[pool]]
  train_df <- test_data_list[[pool]]$train_df

  for (i in seq_len(nrow(vars_df))) {
    key <- paste(pool, vars_df$rank[i])
    pdp_data_list[[key]] <- list(
      pool      = pool,
      var       = vars_df$parent_var[i],
      var_label = vars_df$label[i],
      is_cont   = is.numeric(train_df[[vars_df$parent_var[i]]]),
      pd        = compute_pdp(fit, vars_df$parent_var[i], train_df)
    )
  }
}

# Shared y-axis limits: one range covering all 6 predictors within each pool
y_limits <- lapply(c_data_names_rf, function(pool) {
  range(unlist(lapply(pdp_data_list[paste(pool, 1:6)], \(d) d$pd$yhat)), na.rm = TRUE)
}) |> setNames(c_data_names_rf)

# Pass 2: build plots with shared y limits and consistent theme
pdp_base_theme <- theme_classic(base_size = 11) +
  theme(axis.title = element_text(size = 10),
        axis.text  = element_text(size = 9))

make_pdp_plot <- function(d, y_lims) {
  pd      <- d$pd
  y_label <- if (d$pool == "agc") "AGC (Mg C ha\u207B\u00B9)" else "\u0394SOC (Mg C ha\u207B\u00B9)"

  if (d$is_cont) {
    ggplot(pd, aes(x = x_val, y = yhat)) +
      geom_line(linewidth = 0.7) +
      coord_cartesian(ylim = y_lims) +
      labs(x = d$var_label, y = y_label) +
      pdp_base_theme
  } else {
    pd <- pd |>
      mutate(x_val = as.character(x_val),
             x_val = coalesce(unname(level_display_labels[x_val]), x_val))
    ggplot(pd, aes(x = reorder(x_val, yhat), y = yhat)) +
      geom_point(size = 1.5) +
      coord_cartesian(ylim = y_lims) +
      labs(x = d$var_label, y = y_label) +
      pdp_base_theme +
      theme(axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 45, hjust = 1, size = 7))
  }
}

pdp_plot_list <- lapply(names(pdp_data_list), function(key) {

# Add y-axis label to left-column panels only (ranks 1 and 4); suppress elsewhere
```

## Extreme prediction profiling

Exploratory (figures are displayed only, not saved): compare predictor distributions among training observations with the lowest 10%, middle and highest 10% of model predictions.

```{r extreme-profiling-setup}

# Helper: top N continuous (numeric) predictors for a pool, from the SHAP ranking
get_top_cont_vars <- function(pool, n = 6) {
  train_df <- test_data_list[[pool]]$train_df
  shap_rank |>
    rename(variable = parent_var) |>
    filter(c_pool == pool) |>
    filter(
      variable %in% names(train_df),
      map_lgl(variable, \(v) is.numeric(train_df[[v]]))
    ) |>
    slice_head(n = n) |>
    select(variable, label)
}

# Predict on training data and label extreme groups (P10 / P90 of predictions)
extreme_list <- list()

for (pool in c_data_names_rf) {

  fit      <- fit_list[[pool]]
  train_df <- test_data_list[[pool]]$train_df

  aug <- predict(fit, new_data = train_df) |>
    bind_cols(train_df) |>
    rename(pred = .pred)

  q_lo <- quantile(aug$pred, 0.10)
  q_hi <- quantile(aug$pred, 0.90)

  aug <- aug |>
    mutate(pred_group = factor(
      case_when(
        pred <= q_lo ~ "Low (\u2264P10)",
        pred >= q_hi ~ "High (\u2265P90)",
        TRUE         ~ "Middle"
      ),
      levels = c("Low (\u2264P10)", "Middle", "High (\u2265P90)")
    ))

  extreme_list[[pool]] <- aug
  cat(pool, ": Low n =", sum(aug$pred_group == "Low (\u2264P10)"),
      "| Middle n =", sum(aug$pred_group == "Middle"),
      "| High n =",  sum(aug$pred_group == "High (\u2265P90)"), "\n")
}

```

```{r extreme-cat, fig.width = 12, fig.height = 5}
make_cat_prop_plot <- function(aug, cat_var, var_title, label_map = NULL) {

}
```

## SHAP — interaction heatmap

```{r shap-interaction-heatmap, fig.width = 11, fig.height = 5}

# Helper: attach readable labels to a vector of variable names
attach_labels <- function(vars) {
  tibble(variable = vars) |>
    left_join(dummy_label_map,      by = c("variable" = "dummy_col")) |>
    left_join(predictor_label_lkup, by = c("variable" = "Variable")) |>
    mutate(label = coalesce(label, Label, variable)) |>
    pull(label)
}

inter_plots <- lapply(c_data_names_rf, function(pool) {

  inter_arr <- shap_inter_list[[pool]]$interactions

  # Mean absolute pairwise interaction (exclude main-effect diagonal)
  inter_mat        <- apply(abs(inter_arr), c(1, 2), mean)
  diag(inter_mat)  <- NA

  # Focus on top 15 variables by total off-diagonal interaction
  top_vars <- sort(rowSums(inter_mat, na.rm = TRUE), decreasing = TRUE) |>
    head(15) |> names()

  inter_long <- inter_mat[top_vars, top_vars] |>
    as.data.frame() |>
    rownames_to_column("var1") |>
    pivot_longer(-var1, names_to = "var2", values_to = "interaction") |>
    filter(!is.na(interaction), var1 < var2) |>   # upper triangle only
    mutate(
      label1 = attach_labels(var1),
      label2 = attach_labels(var2)
    )

  # Reorder both axes by total interaction strength.
  # Use union of label1 and label2 so the lexicographically-last variable
  # (which only appears as var2 in the upper triangle) is included in factor levels.
  axis_order <- bind_rows(
    inter_long |> select(label = label1, interaction),
    inter_long |> select(label = label2, interaction)
  ) |>
    group_by(label) |> summarise(tot = sum(interaction)) |>
    arrange(tot) |> pull(label)

  inter_long <- inter_long |>
    mutate(
      label1 = factor(label1, levels = axis_order),
      label2 = factor(label2, levels = rev(axis_order))
    )

  ggplot(inter_long, aes(x = label1, y = label2, fill = interaction)) +
    geom_tile(colour = "white", linewidth = 0.3) +
    scale_fill_viridis_c(name = "Mean\n|interaction|", option = "magma", direction = -1) +
    facet_wrap(~ pool_labels[pool]) +
    labs(x = NULL, y = NULL) +
    theme_classic(base_size = 8) +
    theme(
      axis.text.x      = element_text(angle = 45, hjust = 1, size = 7),
      axis.text.y      = element_text(size = 7),
      strip.background = element_blank(),
      strip.text       = element_text(face = "bold", size = 10),
      legend.text      = element_text(size = 7),
      legend.title     = element_text(size = 7)
    )
})

wrap_plots(inter_plots, ncol = 2) +
  plot_annotation(
    title    = "SHAP pairwise interaction strengths",
    subtitle = "Mean absolute SHAP interaction value; upper triangle; top 15 variables by total interaction"
  )

ggsave(here("output", "figures", "rf_shap_interaction_heatmap.png"),
       wrap_plots(inter_plots, ncol = 2) +
         plot_annotation(title = "SHAP pairwise interaction strengths"),
       width = 11, height = 5, dpi = 300)

```

## SHAP — top interaction pairs

```{r shap-top-pairs}

# Tabulate the strongest pairwise interactions across both pools
top_pairs <- map_dfr(c_data_names_rf, function(pool) {

  inter_arr <- shap_inter_list[[pool]]$interactions
  inter_mat <- apply(abs(inter_arr), c(1, 2), mean)
  diag(inter_mat) <- NA

  as.data.frame(inter_mat) |>
    rownames_to_column("var1") |>
    pivot_longer(-var1, names_to = "var2", values_to = "mean_abs_interaction") |>
    filter(!is.na(mean_abs_interaction), var1 < var2) |>
    mutate(
      label1 = attach_labels(var1),
      label2 = attach_labels(var2),
      c_pool = pool_labels[pool]
    ) |>
    arrange(desc(mean_abs_interaction)) |>
    slice_head(n = 20) |>
    select(c_pool, label1, label2, mean_abs_interaction)
})

top_pairs |>
  mutate(mean_abs_interaction = round(mean_abs_interaction, 3))

write_csv(top_pairs, here("output", "tables", "rf_shap_top_interaction_pairs.csv"))
```

## SHAP — beeswarm plot

```{r shap-beeswarm, fig.width = 11, fig.height = 6}

make_shap_beeswarm <- function(pool, n_vars = 15) {

  shap_mat   <- as.data.frame(shap_list[[pool]]$shaps, check.names = FALSE)
  train_data <- test_data_list[[pool]]$train_df
  outcome_v  <- test_data_list[[pool]]$outcome
  X_baked    <- bake(extract_recipe(fit_list[[pool]]), new_data = train_data) |>
    select(-all_of(outcome_v))

  # Top n variables by mean |SHAP|, in descending order
  top_vars <- colMeans(abs(shap_mat)) |>
    sort(decreasing = TRUE) |>
    head(n_vars) |>
    names()

  shap_long <- shap_mat[, top_vars, drop = FALSE] |>
    mutate(obs = row_number()) |>
    pivot_longer(-obs, names_to = "variable", values_to = "shap_value")

  feat_long <- as.data.frame(X_baked, check.names = FALSE)[, top_vars, drop = FALSE] |>
    mutate(obs = row_number()) |>
    pivot_longer(-obs, names_to = "variable", values_to = "feature_value")

  plot_df <- left_join(shap_long, feat_long, by = c("obs", "variable")) |>
    group_by(variable) |>
    # Rank-based rescaling: distributes colour uniformly across observations
    # regardless of feature distribution (handles skewed variables like age).
    mutate(feature_scaled = scales::rescale(rank(as.numeric(feature_value),
                                                  ties.method = "average"))) |>
    ungroup() |>
    mutate(
      label = attach_labels(variable),
      # Factor ordered so highest-importance variable appears at top of y-axis
      label = factor(label, levels = attach_labels(rev(top_vars)))
    )

  ggplot(plot_df, aes(x = shap_value, y = label, colour = feature_scaled)) +
    geom_vline(xintercept = 0, linewidth = 0.35, linetype = "dashed", colour = "grey50") +
    geom_quasirandom(groupOnX = FALSE, size = 0.45, alpha = 0.55, bandwidth = 0.4) +
    scale_colour_gradient(
      low    = "#3b82f6",
      high   = "#ef4444",
      name   = "Predictor\nvalue",
      breaks = c(0, 1),
      labels = c("Low", "High"),
      guide  = guide_colorbar(barheight = unit(3, "cm"), ticks = FALSE)
    ) +
    labs(title = pool_labels[pool], x = expression("SHAP value" ~ (Mg ~ C ~ ha^{-1})), y = NULL) +
    theme_classic(base_size = 10) +
    theme(
      plot.title         = element_text(face = "bold", hjust = 0.5, size = 11),
      panel.grid.major.x = element_line(colour = "grey92", linewidth = 0.3),
      axis.text.y        = element_text(size = 8),
      axis.text.x        = element_text(size = 8),
      legend.title       = element_text(size = 8),
      legend.text        = element_text(size = 7)
    )
}

bee_agc <- make_shap_beeswarm("agc")
bee_soc <- make_shap_beeswarm("soc")

p_bee_assembled <- bee_agc + bee_soc + plot_layout(guides = "collect")

# Baseline = mean model prediction on training data (reference point for SHAP values)
baselines <- sapply(c_data_names_rf, function(pool) {
  mean(predict(fit_list[[pool]], new_data = test_data_list[[pool]]$train_df)$.pred,
       na.rm = TRUE)
})

p_bee_assembled

ggsave(here("output", "figures", "rf_shap_beeswarm.png"), p_bee_assembled,
       width = 11, height = 6, dpi = 300)
```
